questions.q: What does a scan rule set actually control?
options: Which file types and which classification rules a scan compares your data against
Which users can view a data source
How often a scan repeats
Which sensitivity label gets applied to an asset
questions.explain: A scan rule set is a container of scan rules — it defines which file types are included and which classification rules (system and/or custom) are compared against your data during a scan.

questions.q: What happens if you deselect a file type on the 'Select file types' page when building a scan rule set?
options: That file type is permanently deleted from the source
The scan immediately fails
The file's information is still ingested, but its schema and classifications aren't extracted
Purview blocks all future scans of that source
questions.explain: Deselecting a file type doesn't prevent ingestion — the file's information is still ingested, but schema and classification extraction for that type is skipped.

questions.q: Where can a custom scan rule set be used, once you've created it in a specific domain?
options: Anywhere in the tenant, across every domain
Only inside the domain where it was created
Only by the user who created it
Only on the first scan it's ever attached to
questions.explain: A scan rule set is scoped to the domain it was created in — it can only be used for scans within that same domain.

questions.q: What is a system scan rule set?
options: A rule set you must build manually for every source type
A rule set that only contains custom classifications
A Microsoft-defined scan rule set automatically created for each source type, with every currently available system classification
A rule set that disables classification entirely
questions.explain: System scan rule sets are automatically created by Microsoft for each source type in the catalog, already loaded with every available system classification — and versioned, so you can apply updates.

questions.q: Which of these is a good reason to build a custom scan rule set instead of using the system default?
options: To make the scan run slower on purpose
To include your own custom classifications, which system rule sets can never contain
Because system scan rule sets can't be viewed in the portal
Because custom rule sets apply automatically to every domain
questions.explain: Custom classifications you've created are never part of a system scan rule set — a custom scan rule set is how you make sure they actually get compared against your data during a scan.
